summary: Evald Lidén was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who earned his M.A. at Uppsala University (1883–1895). He was a privatdozent at Uppsala (1895) before serving at the University of Gothenburg as acting professor (1899) and Head (1917–1929).

Evan Thompson is a philosopher who studied at Amherst College under Robert A. F. Thurman and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Toronto (1990) under Francisco Varela. He held posts at Toronto, York University, and the University of British Columbia.
Evelyn Frederick Charles Ludowyk, who worked in history and archaeology, studied at Richmond College. He served as Professor of English at the University of Ceylon from circa 1942 to 1956.

Philosopher Evert Willem Beth studied at Utrecht University from circa 1925 to 1935. He held appointments at the University of Amsterdam from 1946 to 1964 and at Johns Hopkins University from circa 1952 to 1953.

Evgenij Mihajlovič Medvedev worked in Indology and archaeology. He studied at Moscow State University (circa 1951–1956), worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (1956–1957), and became Director at Moscow State University in 1960.

Eviatar Shulman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his BA at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1998–2009), where he became Chairman of the Department of Comparative Religion in 2009.

Eyal Aviv works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He completed his Ph.D. at Harvard University under supervisors Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, with Michael Puett on his committee, and held a position at George Washington University in 2014.

F. B. J. Kuiper worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Utrecht and Leiden (Ph.D. 1934) under Uhlenbeck, van Wijk, Caland, and Vogel. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Leiden (1939–1972).
F. Garritsen was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University under the direction of Jan Gonda.

F. Gelpke studied Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies at the University of Rostock and the University of Göttingen (Dr. phil.), where Emil Sieg supervised him. In 1932, Gelpke served as an assistant at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin.

F. J. Richards was an Indologist and historian who earned his B.A. and M.A. at Exeter College (1893–1902). He founded The Mythic Society in 1909 and served as Honorary Lecturer on Indian Archaeology at SOAS in 1934.

F. M. G. Lorimer was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and historian who studied at Somerville College (1902–1905). She held library posts at the Bodleian Library, the Royal Asiatic Society, and the Royal Horticultural Society.

Fa Qing is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Calgary, where Leslie S. Kawamura was his doctoral supervisor, Anthony W. Barber was interim supervisor, and Xiaojie Yang was his teacher.
Fa Yao is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti. He is attested as a Visiting Lecturer of Theravada Buddhism at the University of Chicago for 2026.

Fabian Wilhelm af Ekenstam was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He earned his Ph.D. at Lund University (1805–1808), held posts there in theology (1809, 1812), and taught philosophy at Katedralskolan, Linköping (1822–1837).

Fabienne Jagou is a scholar of Tibetology and history. She earned her PhD at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences under Pierre-Étienne Will (~1993–1999) and became Maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient around 2001.

Fabio Rambelli is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Ca' Foscari, Naples "L'Orientale", and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. His main posts include Sapporo University (2001–2002) and UC Santa Barbara (from ~2010).

Fabrizia Baldissera is an Indologist who studied at the Department of Mathematics "Federigo Enriques" (1969–2004). She held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and at the University of Florence (circa 2000).

Fabrizio Ferrari is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Ca' Foscari University and earned his PhD at SOAS (2001–2005). He held posts at SOAS (2005–2008), the University of Chester (2008–2018), and the University of Padua (2018).
Fafang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu and served as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.
